resources.string: The 40 and 26-pin headers, the Pico and RP2040-Zero, pin by pin

I²C data of a HAT\'s EEPROM (ID_SD)
I²C clock of a HAT\'s EEPROM (ID_SC)
Every model with 40 pins (A+, B+, 2, 3, 4, 5, Zero). The GPIOs work at 3.3 V and don\'t take 5 V. Pin 1 has the square pad.
Model A and B (rev. 2): the first 26 pins of today\'s 40-pin header. The GPIOs work at 3.3 V. Pin 1 has the square pad.
The first Model B (rev. 1, 2012): pins 3, 5 and 13 are GPIO0, GPIO1 and GPIO21 (I²C0 on 3 and 5), the rest as rev. 2.
RP2040 (Pico, Pico W) and RP2350 (Pico 2, 2 W), seen from above, USB at the top. The GP pins work at 3.3 V; each one\'s functions as its pinout prints them.
Pulled low, it resets the chip
The ADC\'s reference voltage (3.3 V on the board)
3.3 V out, up to about 300 mA
Pulled low, it turns the 3.3 V regulator off
Waveshare\'s, seen from above, USB-C at the top. Its GP pins at 3.3 V, labeled by their GPIO numbers; GP16 drives its RGB LED inside. More pads underneath are not drawn.
